title: WearTrails: watching wear appear on the ground

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Slide a block across the floor, and it leaves a mark. Could a browser draw that mark as it forms?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's WearTrailsExperiments. Antoine built browser prototypes that turn contact and sliding into persistent wear and flow maps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It comes from his master's research at ÉTS on wear in texture space. Instead of a heavy simulator, contact, sliding speed and traction get written straight into a texture, exactly where contact happened.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So you drop a shape and watch?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A cube, sphere, puck, cone or your own model falls on a plane, with gravity, friction and speed you choose. Eight small views show the contact patch, velocity and traction, and the ground gradually records the wear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can export the wear map as an image. It runs with three.js and a physics engine, plus nine single-page experiments. It's open, for graphics researchers who want to try the ideas. The written page has the details.
